snapshot_note: Cumulative snapshot; refreshed when the paper pipeline reruns
source_paper: Della Vedova (2026), 'Detecting Informed Trading in Prediction Markets: One Event at a Time', SSRN 6567238 (revised June 2026)

event_detection.method: Per-event joint-accuracy test against the price-implied null (each position's success probability is its own transaction-time price), Holm-corrected across the events each trader contests, mutually-exclusive (neg-risk) events excluded, and a beta-binomial dependence adjustment at intraclass correlation rho = 0.18.

sample.provenance: paper Section 3 (not derivable from committed stage outputs)

survivors.note: All survivors are all-correct records on disclosure events; reported by archetype only, matching the paper's anonymization.

event_detection.forward_test: The statistic flags the trader charged in CFTC v. Spagnuolo at the five percent level under the estimated within-event dependence; it was first run sixteen days before the complaint. Flags mark statistical patterns consistent with informed trading, not legal determinations.

sustained_skill.reclassification_note: This wallet-level pooled excess-accuracy screen was the April 2026 draft's detector. The June 2026 revision reclassifies it: a statistic that averages a trader's record measures sustained skill and is asymptotically blind to episodic information. It is published here as a skill-persistence monitor, not an informed-trading detector.
sustained_skill.data_note: July 2026 rerun on the corrected master (trades through 2026-07-03; wallets with at least 10 resolved trades).
